subject: ela
cluster: Research to Build and Present Knowledge
intro: Ninth graders gather relevant information from multiple authoritative print and digital sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the usefulness of each source in answering the research question; integrate information into the text selectively; and avoid plagiarism by following a standard citation format. Quoting uses exact words; paraphrasing restates in your own words; both require citation.

items.prompt: What is the difference between QUOTING and PARAPHRASING?

steps: Quoting uses exact words in quotation marks; paraphrasing restates the idea in your own words.
So quoting is word-for-word; paraphrasing is in your own words.
solution.answer: Quoting uses exact words; paraphrasing restates the idea in your own words.

steps: An authoritative source has recognized expertise or credibility.
So it is written by an expert or trusted institution.
solution.answer: It is written by an expert or trusted institution.

steps: You include only what is relevant and useful, avoiding overload.
So you use only the most relevant, useful information.
solution.answer: To use only the most relevant, useful information and avoid overload.

items.prompt: Using exact words in quotation marks is ____.
Restating an idea in your own words is ____.
A source written by an expert is ____.
